Event_Title_MS: Rampasan kuasa di Ghana; tempahan dibatalkan
Description: President Nkrumah was deposed in a coup and the new government cancelled the order, which was costing in the region of £5 million. This left Yarrow with a partly completed ship. The TLDM briefing gives the reason for the cancellation as the ship's high price (£5 million).
Description_MS: Presiden Nkrumah digulingkan dalam rampasan kuasa, lalu kerajaan baharu Ghana membatalkan tempahan kapal yang bernilai kira-kira £5 juta itu. Menurut taklimat TLDM, tempahan dibatalkan kerana harga kapal terlalu mahal.

Description: Yarrow decided to finish the ship in the hope of finding another buyer and launched her without ceremony on 29 December 1966.

Event_Title: Moved to Portsmouth; refitted at Chatham
Event_Title_MS: Dipindahkan ke Portsmouth; dibaik pulih di Chatham
Description: In April 1972 the ship was moved from the Firth of Clyde to Portsmouth Dockyard, and then to Chatham Dockyard, where she was refitted to Royal Navy standards.
Commissioned into the Royal Navy as HMS Mermaid with the pennant number F76.
Historical_Notes: The place of commissioning is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Description: As HMS Mermaid, the ship was based in Singapore in 1974 and 1975 during her Royal Navy service in the Far East.
Description_MS: Sebagai HMS Mermaid, kapal ini berpangkalan di Singapura pada tahun 1974 dan 1975 semasa berkhidmat dengan Tentera Laut Diraja British di Timur Jauh.
Historical_Notes: A Hong Kong newspaper report of a later visit by KD Hang Tuah states that, as HMS Mermaid, she was 'based in Singapore in 1974 and 1975'. When her Far East service began is not confirmed.

Description: On 6 May 1976, during the Cod Wars, HMS Mermaid had an encounter with the Icelandic Coast Guard vessel Baldur. A contemporary photo board records it with the caption 'ICGV Baldur's can opening technique as attempted on H.M.S. Mermaid on 6th May 76'.
Description_MS: Pada 6 Mei 1976, semasa Perang Ikan Kod (Cod Wars), HMS Mermaid berhadapan dengan kapal Pengawal Pantai Iceland, Baldur, dalam satu insiden. Sebuah papan gambar sezaman merakamkan insiden ini dengan kapsyen 'ICGV Baldur's can opening technique as attempted on H.M.S. Mermaid on 6th May 76'.
Historical_Notes: The caption is quoted as written; photographs by G Wicks (not published). The board does not say whether the ships collided or whether Mermaid was damaged; that is still being checked.

Description: The minesweeper HMS Fittleton collided with Mermaid while coming alongside, capsized and sank. Twelve men died, eleven of them Royal Naval Reserve volunteers.
Historical_Notes: The collision happened during a NATO exercise (SRC016), on passage to Hamburg (SRC023). The exact position is not given in the sources reviewed.

Event_Title: Placed in Royal Malaysian Navy service
Description: HMS Mermaid was placed in Royal Malaysian Navy service on 16 May 1977, to be commissioned as KD Hang Tuah with her pennant number, F76, unchanged. She replaced the earlier KD Hang Tuah (F433), the former HMS Loch Insh.
Description_MS: HMS Mermaid mula berkhidmat dalam Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia pada 16 Mei 1977, sebelum ditauliahkan sebagai KD Hang Tuah dengan mengekalkan nombor penant F76. Kapal ini menggantikan KD Hang Tuah (F433) yang terdahulu, iaitu bekas HMS Loch Insh.
Historical_Notes: Original wording (TLDM briefing, p.5): 'HMS MERMAID diletakkan dalam perkhidmatan TLDM pada 16 Mei 77'. New Times Sabah (2007) gives the same date. The commissioning ceremony took place later, on 22 July 1977 (next event). Some earlier sources give April 1977 for the transfer; that date is kept for review.

Event_Title: Commissioned as KD Hang Tuah at Southampton
Event_Title_MS: Ditauliahkan sebagai KD Hang Tuah di Southampton
Description: KD Hang Tuah was commissioned into the Royal Malaysian Navy at Southampton on 22 July 1977, at a handover ceremony that followed naval tradition. The ship was named by Datin Badariah, and the commissioning address was given by her commanding officer, Lt Kol (Laut) Tuan Hashim bin Tuan Mohamed. She was named after Laksamana Hang Tuah, a warrior of Malay history, and kept her pennant number, F76.
Description_MS: KD Hang Tuah ditauliahkan dalam perkhidmatan Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia di Southampton pada 22 Julai 1977 dalam upacara penyerahan yang mengikut tradisi tentera laut. Upacara penamaan kapal disempurnakan oleh Datin Badariah, dan ucapan pentauliahan disampaikan oleh Pegawai Memerintahnya, Leftenan Kolonel (Laut) Tuan Hashim bin Tuan Mohamed. Kapal ini dinamakan sempena Laksamana Hang Tuah dan mengekalkan nombor penant F76.
Historical_Notes: Place and date from the TLDM briefing (p.5) and Utusan Malaysia (19 October 1977); the TLDM album of the ceremony is titled 'Upacara Penamaan dan Pertauliahan KD Hang Tuah di Southamptom' and shows the White Ensign lowered and the Malaysian naval ensign raised (photographs not published). The sources differ on the title of the Malaysian representative and on the size of the first crew; these details are kept for review.

Event_Title_MS: Berlepas dari Portsmouth pulang ke tanah air
Description: KD Hang Tuah began her voyage home at 3.00 pm local time on Monday, 15 August 1977, leaving the British naval dockyard at Portsmouth. The passage took about two months.
During a seven-day stay at Jeddah from 10 to 17 September 1977, Muslim members of the crew were able to perform the Umrah and celebrate Hari Raya Aidilfitri in the Holy Land.

KD Hang Tuah arrived at Port Klang at 9.00 am on 14 October 1977. She was welcomed by the Chief of the Armed Forces, General Tan Sri Ibrahim bin Ismail; the Chief of the Army, General Tan Sri Sany bin Abdul Ghaffar; the Chief of the Navy, Rear Admiral Datuk Mohd Zain bin Mohd Salleh; senior TLDM officers, members of the LLP and Ministry of Defence staff. The Chief of the Armed Forces performed the tepung tawar blessing on board (Utusan Malaysia and Berita Harian, 15 October 1977).
Historical_Notes: Names, ranks and the abbreviation 'LLP' are given as written on the panel ('Laksamana Muda' translated as Rear Admiral). A photograph on the panel shows General Tan Sri Ibrahim bin Ismail performing the tepung tawar blessing on the ship at Port Klang.

Description: The ship called at Malacca on 16 and 17 October 1977 to commemorate the state's history and in honour of her name, before sailing for the TLDM base at Woodlands.

Event_Title: Arrives at TLDM Woodlands base, Singapore
Event_Title_MS: Tiba di Pangkalan TLDM Woodlands, Singapura
Description: On 18 October 1977 KD Hang Tuah berthed at the jetty of the TLDM base at Woodlands, Singapore, where the navy remained until its move to Lumut in 1984. She was welcomed by the Naval Region I commander, Commodore P. K. Nettur, the commanding officer of KD Malaya, M. W. Alvisse, and the families of the crew.
Historical_Notes: Names as written on the panel: 'Panglima Wilayah Laut I, Komodor P.K. Nettur' and 'Pegawai Memerintah KD MALAYA, Kolonel M. W. Alvisse' (rank 'Kolonel' as written).

Description: KD Hang Tuah visited Kuching, berthing at the Datuk Amar Sim Kheng Hong Port at Pending. It was her second visit since 1977. A newspaper report described her as responsible for sea training and patrol duties.
Description_MS: KD Hang Tuah melawat Kuching dan bersandar di Pelabuhan Datuk Amar Sim Kheng Hong, Pending. Ini ialah lawatan keduanya sejak 1977. Laporan akhbar menyatakan bahawa kapal ini bertanggungjawab untuk tugas latihan laut dan rondaan.
Historical_Notes: The dates (5–9 May 1983) are written by hand on the album page above the clipping; the newspaper's title and date are not visible. The commanding officer named, Nik Anis bin Nik Abdullah, commanded until 25 May 1983 (TLDM list).

Event_Title: Carries the navy's royal colours from Woodlands to Lumut
Event_Title_MS: Membawa panji-panji Diraja TLDM dari Woodlands ke Lumut
Description: As the TLDM moved its headquarters from Woodlands to Lumut, the navy's royal colours (panji-panji Diraja) were transferred to the new KD Malaya at Lumut by the Fleet Materiel Commander, Captain Khoo Tee Chuan, travelling aboard KD Hang Tuah.
Historical_Notes: From the TLDM website, which names the ship only as 'KD HANG TUAH'. It is identified as this ship because the earlier KD Hang Tuah (ex-HMS Loch Insh) left service in 1977 (SRC024).

Event_Title: Training cruise to the South Pacific
Description: KD Hang Tuah left Malaysia on 24 June 1985 on a training cruise that took her to Darwin, Suva, Nuku'alofa and Port Moresby. The Fiji Sun described her as the first Malaysian naval ship to visit the South Pacific.
Description_MS: KD Hang Tuah meninggalkan Malaysia pada 24 Jun 1985 untuk pelayaran latihan ke Darwin, Suva, Nuku'alofa dan Port Moresby. Akhbar Fiji Sun menyifatkannya sebagai kapal tentera laut Malaysia pertama yang melawat Pasifik Selatan.
Historical_Notes: The dates of the calls at Darwin, Suva and Nuku'alofa are not given in the clippings reviewed.

Description: On her way home from Tonga, KD Hang Tuah began a four-day visit to Port Moresby on 31 July 1985. The Post-Courier described her as the first modern military ship to visit Papua New Guinea.
Description_MS: Dalam pelayaran pulang dari Tonga, KD Hang Tuah memulakan lawatan selama empat hari ke Port Moresby pada 31 Julai 1985. Akhbar Post-Courier menyifatkannya sebagai kapal tentera moden pertama yang melawat Papua New Guinea.

Description: During Docking Essential Defect (DED) repairs at Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd, the ship's 1940s-technology Admiralty Standard Range engines (eight ASR1 16 VTS main engines and four ASR1 8 LTS generators) were found worn, with genuine spare parts hard to obtain. In August 1994 a ministerial meeting approved the TLDM's proposal to fit new engines.
Historical_Notes: The panel text is cut off at the right edge in the photograph; the year of the docking after '1 September' is not visible. The panel names the meeting 'Mesyuarat Lembaga Menteri' (wording partly cut off). It also notes that spare parts supplied without certificates of origin were returned to the supplier.

Event_Title: Towed to Pasir Gudang for re-engining
Event_Title_MS: Ditunda ke Pasir Gudang untuk pengenjinan semula
Description: The ship was towed to Malaysia Shipyard & Engineering (MSE), now Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Sdn Bhd, at Pasir Gudang, Johor, where the re-engining was carried out.

Event_Title: Re-engined ship accepted by the TLDM
Event_Title_MS: Kapal diterima semula oleh TLDM selepas pengenjinan semula
Description: The re-engining, which cost RM24 million, was completed and the ship was accepted by the TLDM in February 1997.

Event_Title: Last year of the Limbo Mk10 mortar
Description: According to the TLDM briefing, 2000 was the last year in which the ship's Limbo Mk10 anti-submarine mortar, mounted on the flight deck, was operated.
Description_MS: Menurut taklimat TLDM, tahun 2000 ialah tahun terakhir mortar antikapal selam Limbo Mk10 kapal ini, yang terletak di geladak penerbangan, beroperasi.
Historical_Notes: Original wording (p.10): 'Tahun 2000 merupakan tahun terakhir bagi pengoperasian sistem Mortar Limbo Mk10'.

Event_Title: Visit to Ho Chi Minh City
Event_Title_MS: Lawatan ke Bandar Raya Ho Chi Minh
Description: KD Hang Tuah led three Royal Malaysian Navy ships, with KD Kelewang and KD Kris, on a three-day visit to Ho Chi Minh City, berthing at Saigon Port on 26 July 2000. The Saigon Times described her as a training ship for reserve officers.
Description_MS: KD Hang Tuah mengetuai tiga buah kapal Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia, bersama KD Kelewang dan KD Kris, dalam lawatan selama tiga hari ke Bandar Raya Ho Chi Minh dan bersandar di Pelabuhan Saigon pada 26 Julai 2000. Akhbar The Saigon Times menyifatkannya sebagai kapal latihan bagi pegawai simpanan.
Historical_Notes: The report (27 July 2000) says the ships berthed 'yesterday'.

Description: The Captain's Barge and the Sea Boat Whaler, in use for almost 35 years, were replaced by 7.62 m rigid inflatable boats (RHIBs) in October 2001.
Description_MS: Captain's Barge dan Sea Boat Whaler, yang telah digunakan hampir 35 tahun, digantikan dengan Rigid Inflatable Boat (RHIB) 7.62 m pada Oktober 2001.
Historical_Notes: Original wording (TLDM briefing, p.13): 'Penukaran Sea Boat Whaler dan Captain Barge kepada 7.62M Rigid Inflatable Boat (RHIB) pada Okt 01'.

Description: The training ship KD Hang Tuah anchored at Sandakan on 24 September 2007 for a two-day visit and was opened to the public at the naval base before leaving for Tawau. Her commanding officer was Cdr Yee Tai Peng.
Description_MS: Kapal latihan KD Hang Tuah berlabuh di Sandakan pada 24 September 2007 untuk lawatan selama dua hari dan dibuka kepada orang awam di pangkalan tentera laut sebelum belayar ke Tawau. Pegawai Memerintahnya ialah Komander Yee Tai Peng.
Historical_Notes: The report (Tuesday, 25 September 2007) says the ship anchored on Monday and would leave for Tawau the next day. The figures it gives for speed, crew and dimensions differ from the TLDM briefing and are not used.

Event_Title: Op Fajar deployment to the Gulf of Aden
Event_Title_MS: Penugasan Op Fajar ke Teluk Aden
Description: On 4 February 2009 KD Hang Tuah sailed from Lumut for Op FAJAR 03/2008, the TLDM operation to escort Malaysian merchant ships safely through the Gulf of Aden, where ships were being seized by pirates. She took over the task from KD Sri Indera Sakti and returned to Lumut on 14 May 2009, 100 days after sailing.
Description_MS: Pada 4 Februari 2009 KD Hang Tuah belayar dari Lumut untuk Op FAJAR 03/2008, operasi TLDM bagi mengiringi kapal-kapal dagang milik Malaysia dengan selamat melalui Teluk Aden, tempat kapal-kapal dirampas oleh lanun. Kapal ini mengambil alih tugas tersebut daripada KD Sri Indera Sakti dan kembali ke Lumut pada 14 Mei 2009, 100 hari selepas belayar.
Historical_Notes: From a first-hand account by a TLDM officer on board, 'Noktah Pelayaran Op FAJAR 03/2008' (pp.2, 4, 5 and 16). Operational details are not published.

Description: At a ceremony at Lumut naval base, the Chief of Navy, Admiral Tan Sri Ahmad Kamarulzaman Ahmad Badaruddin, declared KD Hang Tuah, then the oldest ship in the fleet, the TLDM's museum ship. She remained in commission. By then she had sailed some 500,000 km.
Historical_Notes: Bernama reported that Boustead Naval Shipyard and the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture would carry out the conversion, with opening then expected in early 2019.

Description: The TLDM briefing records that the ship's slipping was completed on 5 September 2022.
Description_MS: Taklimat TLDM merekodkan bahawa kerja slipping kapal ini selesai pada 5 September 2022.
Historical_Notes: Original wording (p.19): 'GAMBAR KAPAL SELESAI SLIPPING PADA 5 SEP 22'. Where the work was done is not stated.

Description: KD Hang Tuah was decommissioned in a military ceremony at Lumut naval base after nearly five decades of Malaysian service. The Western Fleet Commander, Vice Admiral Datuk Baharudin Wan Md Nor, officiated; the ship's bell was rung and her ensign lowered for the last time. The decommissioning formed part of the TLDM's '15 to 5' fleet transformation programme.

Event_Title: Handed over to the Perak state government
Description: At a ceremony at Himpitan 1, Lumut naval base, the TLDM handed the ship to the Perak state government, represented by the Menteri Besar, Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad, for conversion into the Memorial Muzium Kapal Diraja Hang Tuah. The project is a public–private partnership between Menteri Besar Incorporated (MB Inc.) and Aero Art Sdn Bhd; its first phase is budgeted at RM30 million.
